# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 12
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 12

---

*[Thomas's final acts of ministry. Tertia, the wife of the king's son, is converted. The king orders Thomas arrested for the last time.]*

1. And in those days there was another woman whose name was Tertia, the wife of Misdaeus the king's son. And she heard of Thomas and came to him.

2. And she listened to his teaching and was convinced by him and believed and was baptized.

3. And she also forsook the bed of her husband Misdaeus.

4. And Misdaeus went to his father the king and told him of the things that Thomas had done.

5. And the king was exceedingly wroth and he sent soldiers to seize Thomas.

6. And when Thomas was seized, many of those who had believed were troubled, and they wept.

7. And Thomas said to them: "Do not weep. My Lord is strong and he is able to do all things. And he will bring out of prison those who are his."

8. And they came and brought him before the king.

9. And the king said to Thomas: "What evil have you done to my son and to Charisius?"

10. And Thomas said: "I have done them no evil. Rather, I have proclaimed to them the living God and the eternal life."

11. And the king said: "By doing this you have caused discord in our kingdom."

12. And Thomas said: "The discord is not mine. Truth brings its own opposition from those who love darkness."

13. And the king said: "Condemn yourself and see that your teaching does not lead others astray."

14. And Thomas said: "The truth cannot be condemned by those who have not received it."

15. And the king was angry and commanded that Thomas be put in prison until he decided what to do with him.

16. And Thomas went gladly, praising God.

17. And many followed him even to the prison, and he taught them there.

18. And among those who came was Mygdonia, and Thomas gave her instructions.

19. And he said to the others who were gathered: "Brethren, stand firm in the faith. For my Lord Jesus Christ is with you, and he will not forsake those who believe in him."

20. And he laid his hands on them and blessed them and departed within.

---
*EMET note: Tertia's conversion and sexual renunciation (v.3) precisely repeats Mygdonia's pattern. The ATH presents a consistent vision: holy women, moved by Thomas's preaching, renounce marital sexual relations. This caused the text to be condemned by some church fathers as promoting family dissolution.*
